epic.title: Future: Managed KaleidoSphere remote connector / MCP discovery
epic.scope: Close the FRC.0-FRC.4 discovery program without implementation, procurement, endpoint, API, credential, customer-data, deployment, activation, support, compliance-readiness, production-readiness, or runtime authority.
reasons: All five discovery children are publicly closed and bound to serial public releases, and every child terminates REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE or NO_GO rather than authorizing implementation.

The released evidence leaves product, architecture, tenant-isolation, security, privacy, license, data-owner, custody, egress, legal, compliance, operations, support, cost, rollback, and final implementation approvals or proofs absent.
Local validation, focused tests, schema conformance, fixtures, commits, and PACKAGE_DONE are package evidence only and cannot substitute for public closure or implementation authority.
epic.completionRule: The parent discovery closes exactly REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE because #89-#93 are publicly CLOSED on released main commits and #93 records terminal REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE with execution NO_GO. Discovery completion is not implementation approval.
epic.supersession: Only a separately authorized immutable work item may reconsider one bounded implementation proposal after independently owned evidence closes every applicable released blocker and Jo, Product, and Security each grant explicit proposal-specific authorization. Reconsideration does not itself authorize implementation.

criteria.text: Threat model and authority/data-flow diagram.
Build/buy/reject decision with cost, compliance and support assumptions.
Explicit implementation blockers and required approvals.
Authority matrix.
Revocation and replay scenarios.
Receipt-signing threat model and key custody options.
Explicit approval gates for any later implementation.
Data classification and retention matrix.
Tenant-isolation and egress threat model.
Secret-custody options with explicit reject/approve gates.
Compliance assumptions and unknowns.
Spike plan with start/stop/rollback criteria.
Synthetic fixtures and isolation plan.
Go/no-go criteria for whether a spike is even worth running.
Decision memo cites the discovery artifacts.
Risks, costs, compliance gaps, support burden and rollback are explicit.
Any implementation child is blocked on separate explicit authorization.
Discovery artifacts are explicit, linked, and preserve their FUTURE_BACKLOG historical label.
Threat model and authority/data-flow diagram exist before any spike decision.
Synthetic spike plan has success, stop and rollback criteria and was not run without explicit authorization.
#93 records REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE and NO_GO with released evidence.

parentAcceptance.evidence: Issues #89-#93 are publicly CLOSED/completed and releases 2026_08_30_v1 through 2026_08_30_v5 bind their serial main SHAs.
All 21 child and parent discovery criteria bind current-checkout artifacts and released child provenance.
Jo's released #93 decision records REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE and NO_GO; this parent adopts that exact terminal disposition.

The parent closes discovery only and explicitly denies implementation, procurement, endpoint, API widening, credentials/customer data, deployment, activation, compliance-readiness, and production-readiness authority.

mandatoryNegatives.condition: Any child #89-#93 is missing or not publicly closed with its exact release/main binding.
A local PACKAGE_DONE, focused test, commit, PR, CI result, or merge is presented as public issue closure.
Discovery completion, planning validation, or the parent terminal decision is presented as implementation or procurement approval.
An endpoint, hosted service, SaaS, remote MCP, public bind, or transport is created, selected, discovered, or claimed.
Credentials, secrets, tokens, customer data, provider payloads, raw rows, or live identity data are requested, supplied, processed, or claimed.
External API v2 gains a seventh intent or any of status, discovery, analyze, plan, preview, or readback is semantically widened.
Deployment, activation, compliance-readiness, production-readiness, customer-readiness, service level, or operational support is inferred or claimed.

provenance.method: Read-only GitHub issue/release/tag readback plus current-checkout artifact validation; no .git history required by the focused test.
provenance.note: The parent issue was still publicly open at reconciliation. This artifact supplies the terminal decision for later integration/delivery; it does not claim that the parent issue, PR, release, or queue is already closed.
